dedupe_keys.name: hygrothermal measurements of 56 timber framed wall structures and material properties

description: This dataset gives laboratory measurements for 56 timber-framed wall structures over autumn, winter and spring conditions, with the properties of their materials, as a benchmark for validating hygrothermal simulation software. It was published on Zenodo on 2 December 2025 by Antti Mikkonen and Juha Vinha of Tampere University, Finland. For each wall it provides geometry, temperatures and relative humidities with initial and boundary values, and material properties that vary with relative humidity, such as sorption curves; long descriptive variable names and machine-readable JSON aim at large-scale automated validation, with previews and schematics for people. Coverage: laboratory test walls representing Nordic timber-frame construction. Access: zipped wall-structure and material files (about 36 MB) and a readme, openly downloadable. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: laboratory boundary conditions, not in-service buildings. Simulation uses are validating moisture and heat transfer models used to assess mould and decay risk in walls under changing climates and retrofits. Related records: the Finnish residential material inventory and the Norway roof snow load measurements.
